name: One-way linear-motion qualifier
summary: A linear-motion qualifier identifies movement or force in one documented direction.
description: A linear-motion qualifier identifies movement or force in one documented direction. The arrow describes a mechanical movement or force along a line. The same logical relationship can be drawn in another orientation without changing the mechanism.
Distinguish movement arrows from electrical continuation arrows by their context and association with the mechanism. A movement diagram should name the driven element and reference its positions.
readingNotes: Orient the indication to the actual diagram relationship; do not treat its drawing direction as an equipment compass bearing.
Rotating the same motion indication does not create another engineering function.
drawingChecklist: Identify the associated device, circuit or diagram boundary.
Orient the indication to the actual diagram relationship; do not treat its drawing direction as an equipment compass bearing.
Cross-reference the equipment data, terminal mapping or operating-state legend needed to interpret the form.
distinction: Rotating the same motion indication does not create another engineering function.
